run: step 2 of the pronunciation fix: OmniVoice on plain script against three marked forms of the same text, written by the front-end the text-only comparison chose, judged blind by ear
status: registered 2026-10-03, before the front-end ran on these sentences and before any render
why: the pronunciation review found OmniVoice's errors on plain script are mostly ezafe and short vowels, and that it reads the marks it is given; the text-only comparison (eval/runs/persian-voice-frontend-components-v1.json) chose hazm's ParsBERT tagger for the ezafe and ruled out marking every word's vowels. This asks whether writing those marks in makes OmniVoice read better
question: does each kind of mark - the ezafe, a sukun where no ezafe belongs, first short vowels - lower the words a native listener hears said wrong

sentences.written_by: Claude, 2026-10-03, before the front-end ran on them: ezafe chains (heads ending in a consonant, a silent h, a vowel), nouns right before a verb, number or adjective that take no ezafe (the review's traps), first syllables with short vowels (fatha, kasra, damma), a homograph, colloquial, news and a long sentence
sentences.leakage_check: none of the 12 found in HomoRich (528,875), SentenceBench (400) or the adaptation split - letters only, equal or one inside the other with at least 20 letters and half the longer
sentences.not_reused: none of the review's 14 sentences, which are development material

front_end.ezafe: hazm's ParsBERT tagger (roshan-research/hazm-parsbert-postagger @ eba1d2b30cc48206c0144b36d2b663652d44faf9) through hazm 0.12.1 with full tags; a tag with ,EZ is an ezafe; the word's tag also gives its part of speech
front_end.readings: KaamelDict (sha256 d5f6982ba93d94d8de19bceac2d0c843857a0b2ea751e9e1c3876fc0514d22c9) looked up by spelling, then the part before a ZWNJ, then without a final clitic (ها، های، م، ت، ش، ...); a reading is used only where every listed reading agrees on the mark it would set
front_end.marks: src/voiceclone/text/marks_fa.py (sha256 b2b82370a1e69a04bfe290b4e24c0613734d322c8317d507ab7031e7bd6c8395, tests/test_marks_fa.py): an ezafe is a kasra on a final consonant or a pronounced final h, ٔ on a silent final h, ی after a final ا/آ/و; a sukun closes a final consonant; a first vowel is fatha, kasra or damma on the first letter, only when the script leaves that vowel unwritten. A word already marked where a mark would go is left alone
front_end.code: scripts/build_frontend_texts.py (the decisions and the four texts, in the frontend environment) -> eval/runs/frontend-listening-v1/texts.json

conditions.A: the plain sentence - what the app sends today
conditions.E: A + every ezafe the tagger predicts, written in
conditions.EN: E + a sukun on each noun, adjective or number the tagger gives no ezafe, when the next word is a noun, adjective, number, verb, adverb, pronoun or determiner
conditions.ENV: EN + the first short vowel of each noun and adjective whose readings agree on it

rendering.engine: OmniVoice through the app (scripts/render_frontend_conditions.py), on this Mac, with the A/B/C run's settings from the app config: seed 42, one take, evaluation off while rendering, the memory guard on (6 GB must be free)
rendering.voice: the Mana-TTS reference of the review (eval/corpus mana_000.wav), so the voice is the same as before
rendering.marks_reach_the_model: every input goes through the app's text pipeline before any engine loads; the run stops if a mark would be changed or dropped, and the manifest keeps the exact strings fed
rendering.cer: after the engine is unloaded, the app's recogniser (faster-whisper large-v3-turbo) against the plain sentence with diacritics stripped - a harm check only, since the script writes neither ezafe nor short vowels and CER cannot see them

review.listener: the user, a native speaker, blind to which reading is which
review.page: as the pronunciation review: one sentence per screen, the plain sentence on top, four readings in hidden slots, each with its words to tap when said wrong or an 'every word right' button and a note, then which reading was best
review.blind: slots from Latin squares (scripts/build_pronunciation_review.py --rotations): each condition in each slot three times; anonymous file names; every render of a sentence matched to one loudness by gain (-26 LUFS, 16-bit); the key outside the page

analysis_fixed_before_listening.code: scripts/score_pronunciation_review.py: per condition, readings with no marked word, words marked wrong out of words, times picked best; the same by category; every marked word with its note
analysis_fixed_before_listening.classification: after reading through the key, Claude sorts the marked words by kind (ezafe, vowel, other) from the listener's notes, as in the review - reported, not used for the decision

decision_rules.steps: A -> E -> EN -> ENV, each compared with the one before it: a step is kept if it lowers the number of words marked wrong; a tie or a rise drops it - marks must earn their place
decision_rules.harm: a step whose mean CER is more than 2 points above the one before it is flagged and not adopted without the user's say, even if the rule above keeps it
decision_rules.into_the_app: the app's front-end takes the marks of every kept step. A combination never rendered (say the ezafe and vowels without the sukun) is not claimed and is rendered and heard before it ships
decision_rules.best_picks: reported beside the counts, with the listener's notes

not_claimed: one listener, one voice, one seed and 147 words written by Claude: a development decision for the front-end, not a measure of the app's pronunciation; other voices are untested
cost: local: OmniVoice took 12-16 s a render in the A/B/C run, so about 15 minutes for 48; the recogniser afterwards, alone. No GPU quota

amendment_2026_10_03_marks_check.when: after the four texts were written and before any render: the first run stopped at the check, before an engine loaded
amendment_2026_10_03_marks_check.what: the check compared whole strings, stricter than registered: it stopped because the app's normaliser writes تأخیر as تاخیر (src/voiceclone/text/normalize_fa.py maps أ to ا), in n09 and in all four of its conditions alike. It now checks what was registered - every mark reaching the model on its word - and lists the app's other changes in the manifest
amendment_2026_10_03_marks_check.found_on_the_way: the same map is why the review's A read تأخیر as taa'khir: OmniVoice was given تاخیر, a long a. The normaliser also turns ۀ (a written ezafe) into a bare ه, dropping the ezafe. Both are app fixes for after this test; here every condition gets the same normalised text, and the front-end writes the ezafe as هٔ, which survives

amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.when: after the Mac run was refused by the memory guard (it stopped while the engine was loading: no render was made, and the partial manifest was deleted) and before anything was sent to Kaggle
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.why: the Mac had 5.1 GB available and OmniVoice's guard needs 6 (the registered setting); the user chose Kaggle over closing apps (2026-10-03). The guard is not overridden
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.what_changes: the machine only: one Kaggle T4 x2 session (marsmanam/persian-voice-frontend-listening-run), the OmniVoice worker on CUDA instead of Metal, in float16 as on the Mac (the configured dtype, which the worker loads on both)
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.what_stays: the app code (the code dataset marsmanam/persian-voice-frontend-listening is staged from the commit that adds this amendment; against the copy the sealed test ran, src/voiceclone differs only by text/marks_fa.py), the texts (texts.json sha256 06fd5f36cc1f2cb41a57c105b808dc3dc4dc836f3f01a574925b82f6598e197b, checked in the notebook before anything renders), the voice (mana_000.wav), seed 42, one take, evaluation off while rendering, the generation settings from the app config, and the weights: k2-fsa/OmniVoice @ c5fdb5ccb189668d56333f77ba2629f4cd7535f4 - the revision in the Mac's cache - fetched with its audio tokenizer's sha256 checked
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.comparison: all 48 render in one session on one GPU, so the four forms of a sentence still differ only in their text. Nothing is compared with a Mac render: a T4 render is not sample-identical to one on Metal
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.environment: OmniVoice's pinned stack (torch 2.8.0+cu128, transformers 5.3.0, omnivoice @ 08be0b4c) and the scoring packages, through the environment cell every OmniVoice session used (kaggle/build_frontend_listening_kernel.py)
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.memory_guard: acts on macOS only (src/voiceclone/memory.py); on Kaggle nothing loads beside the worker while it renders, as on the Mac
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.cer: unchanged: the app's recogniser (faster-whisper large-v3-turbo) after the worker is released, in the same session, on the GPU
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.cost: one session: about half a GPU-hour expected, the render step stopped at 60 minutes; the week's quota stood at 30 GPU-hours, none used (kaggle quota, 2026-10-03)
amendment_2026_10_03_render_on_kaggle.after: the manifest and wavs are fetched into eval/runs/frontend-listening-v1/; the review page and the scoring are as registered
